title: Cyberspace Defense Warrant Officer
raw_text:
8-255S. MOS 255S—Cyberspace Defense Warrant Officer
a. Licensing/certification requirement. CompTIA Security+ CE (meets DoD 8570.01-M
IAT Level II and IAM Level I requirements).
b. Prerequisites. DA Pam 611-21.
c. MOS 255S. MOS 255S is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is any MOS.
All enlisted MOS to include other military services who can substantiate their
qualifications with performance evaluations, awards, and certificates in the Information
Technology (IT) field in cyber security, computer network defense, information systems
administration, local and wide area networks (LAN & WAN), and/or voice and data
internetworking as assessed through the accession process meets current
requirements.
d. Associated SQIs.
   (1) 0--No special qualifications.
   (2) 8--Instructor.
   (3) P--Parachutist.
   (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
   (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
e. Associated ASIs. List is not all inclusive refer to Table 6-6 Listing of universal ASI’s
associated with all warrant officer MOS. Q6--Protection Cell Operations (personnel only)
(Effective 202410).
f. Qualifications.
   (1) WO1/CW2 must--
       (a) Be a U.S. citizen.
       (b) Must qualify for and maintain a Top Secret (TS) clearance with Special
Compartmentalized Information (SCI) access. MOS 255S warrant officers will initiate
procedures to obtain the proper level of clearance immediately upon notification of the
MOS 255S functional designation.
       (c) Meet vision and hearing standards of AR 40-501 for assignment of officers to
Signal Corps, normal color discrimination per AR 40-501, and have full use of both
hands.
       (d) Successfully complete the MOS 255S Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC).
       (e) Minimum OPAT scores for physical demands category moderate (gold) are:
Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD)
- 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles.
       (f) DoD 8570.01-M CNDSP Analyst and IAM Level II certifications are desired.
   (2) CW3 must--
       (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f (1).
       (b) CW2s assigned to CW3 positions will be a graduate of MOS 255S Warrant
Officer Advance Course (WOAC) prior to assignment.
       (c) DoD 8570.01-M CNDSP Auditor and Information Security certifications are
desired.
   (3) CW4 must--
       (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f (2).
       (b) CW3s assigned to CW4 positions will be a graduate of WOILE prior to
assignment.
        (c) DoD 8570.01-M CNDSP Incident Responder and IAM Level III certifications
are desired.
   (4) CW5 must see MOS 255Z.
g. Duties.
   (1) WO1/CW2--
       (a) Design, build, configure, operate, and maintain cybersecurity capabilities and
the implementation of a defensible network architecture in support of cyber operations
internal defensive measures within the DODIN in order to enumerate, illuminate, locate,
eradicate threats and respond to unauthorized activity, security alerts, attempted
exploitation, data exfiltration, escalation, and any additional threats to mission
command.
       (b) Implements cybersecurity policies at all echelons, direct internal defensive
measures across the integrated enterprise and tactical network, assist in cryptographic
network (cryptonet) planning and supports Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations
(EMSO) to reduce detection by electronic signature.
       (c) Advises the commander or Signal operations officer on the management and
operation of Army cybersecurity efforts to include the identification of key terrain,
mission critical networks, nodes, applications and systems while operating within
optimal, degraded, intermittent, or latent environments.
       (d) May serve as an Cyberspace Defense Warrant Officerin a Brigade Combat
Team, Multi-functional Support Brigade, Cyberwarfare Support Battalion, Security
Forces Assistance Brigade, or Functional Support Brigade.
   (2) CW3--
       (a) Directs and performs duties described in paragraph g (1).
       (b) Trains and supervises cybersecurity personnel in the building, configuring,
securing, defending, protecting, and sustaining cybersecurity equipment to maintain a
protected network environment thus enabling combat power projection in all warfighting
domains.
       (c) Advises senior staff members, decision, and policy makers on cybersecurity
efforts to include the identification of key terrain, mission critical networks, nodes,
applications and systems while operating within optimal, degraded, intermittent, or latent
environments.
       (d) May serve as an Cyberspace Defense Warrant Officerin Theater Tactical
     Signal
or Military Intelligence Brigades.
       (e) May serve as an Cyberspace Defense Warrant Officerin Division, ASCC, Multi-
Domain Task Force, or Joint staff organizations.
       (f) May serve as an Instructor/Writer, Doctrine or Capabilities Developer in an
Army or Joint service school.
       (g) May serve as an Cyberspace Defense Warrant Officerat a Regional Cyber
Center, DISA, or National or Joint Training Center.
       (h) May serve as senior Cyberspace Defense Warrant Officerin Special
assignments.
         (i) May serve as the HRC SC Junior WO Assignments Manager or WOCC TAC
Officer.
   (3) CW4--
       (a) Directs and performs duties described in paragraph g (2).
       (b) Provides technical guidance and advice to commanders and staffs on the
management and operation of Army, Joint, intergovernmental, interagency, and
multinational cybersecurity efforts to include the identification of key terrain, mission
critical networks, nodes, applications and systems while operating within optimal,
degraded, intermittent, or latent environments.
       (c) May serve as senior Cyberspace Defense Warrant Officerof
Corps/ASCC/ACOM/Joint staff.
       (d) May serve as senior Cyberspace Defense Warrant Officerfor Theater Signal
CMD staff, DISA, Regional Cyber Center, JITC, or WHCA.
       (e) May serve as senior Cyberspace Defense Warrant Officeras a Doctrine Writer
or
Capabilities Developer.
       (f) May serve as the HRC SC Senior WO Assignments Manager or in Nominative
Assignments.
   (4) CW5 must see MOS 255Z.
h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
    (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
    (2) Table 8-255S-1. Physical requirements.
    (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of three definable skill
levels: W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; and W4 equals CW4. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables:
        (a) Table 8-255S-1. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
        (b) Table 8-255S-2. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
